attribution: Credited to the work the manuscript cites, not to OpenAI or the manuscript's authors. The manuscript says: “This is the smooth, zero-boundary, rank-one case of [14, Theorem 4.1]; Ou’s generic-nefness theorem [19, Theorem 1.4] is an antecedent of the cotangent result.” Its bibliography: “[14] Vladimir Lazić, Shin-ichi Matsumura, Thomas Peternell, Nikolaos Tsakanikas, and Zhixin Xie. The nonvanishing problem for varieties with nef anticanonical bundle. Documenta Mathematica, 28(6):1393– 1440, 2023.” Its bibliography: “[19] Wenhao Ou. On generic nefness of tangent sheaves. Mathematische Zeitschrift, 304:Paper No. 58, 2023.” Quoted from openai/math (Apache-2.0); AMVO has not consulted or checked the cited work.
scope: Theorem 4.1 (Cotangent subsheaves) of the manuscript “Invariant anticanonical indices and conversion of twisted differentials” (preprints/Invariant-anticanonical-indices-and-conversion-of-twisted-differentials-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 068 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c40b47629aa1aa95), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let S be smooth projective with −KS nef. If a line bundle M is a saturated subsheaf of (Ω1 S)⊗b, where b > 0, then −M is pseudoeffective.
